title: Transferring the fast optimum added 0.021 mean residual at a 20 ms readout in selected Allen mouse input models
abstract: We tested whether an inhibitory gain optimized for unfiltered voltage responses remains optimal at a filtered readout. Models used 57 selected excitatory and inhibitory input pairs at 47 mouse VisP targets in Allen Synaptic Physiology r2.1. At a 20 ms exponential readout, transfer of the unfiltered optimum added a mean 0.02123 of filtered excitatory response energy to the residual. The conditional 95% interval across 43 inferred donors was 0.01419 to 0.02955. Aligned onsets and interior decay fits kept the interval above a chosen 0.01 scale. A smaller distance-matched subset did not clearly exceed that scale. Independent frequency integration checked all 342 primary overlap values with relative differences below 8.6e-8. This extends an existing finite-rise cohort model. Separate recordings, assumed linear addition, fitted kernels, inferred donor labels and an assumed downstream filter limit biological inference. No live-circuit cancellation or representation deficit was measured. Original code, aggregate evidence, a figure, source hashes and external regeneration steps support reproduction. External records are not bundled.

display.caption: Gain-transfer costs under assumed exponential readouts. Points are equal-donor means; bars are conditional 95% bootstrap intervals. The dotted 0.01 line is a chosen reporting scale.
